UX Case Study

It's not
"I can't cook."
It's "I'm too tired."

Easey is a food app that doesn't try to teach you to cook. It just tells you what to make with what you already have, with no endless scrolling and no extra pressure. It's for those days when your brain feels fried and takeout starts looking like the only option.

Role
Product Designer
Platform
iOS Mobile App
Type
Concept Project

Option A

Option B
Use easey. Scan fridge, get 1 recipe. Simple.
01. The Problem

Understanding the user's emotional state around cooking.

"I don't know what to make."

It's not about lacking skill, it's decision fatigue. Staring into the fridge hoping a meal spontaneously appears is a universal experience.

"I only have this, this and this. Now what?"

People have random items left in the fridge and don't know how to combine them without it tasting weird.

"All the recipes call for exotic ingredients."

Most recipe apps assume you have a fully stocked pantry. Users just want to use what they ALREADY have.

03. Visual Identity

Why the bowl? Why this logo?

Changing the aesthetics
of food waste.

I wanted a logo that looked welcoming, warm, and zero-pressure. A happy bowl waiting to be filled.

A bowl naturally combines all random ingredients together into something delicious. It felt approachable and easy-going. It literally smiles at you, removing the stress of cooking.

Headings & Body

Ideation: Typography & Colour

Every choice has a reason

Typography Rationale
Headings
Poppins
Clean, modern and calm, without feeling too techy. It gives the app a softer, more reassuring vibe.
Body / UI
Inter
Highly readable at small sizes, pairs naturally with Poppins. Same structural harmony.
Avoided
Rounded sans (too playful)
System UI (too generic)
Colour Rationale
Cream #F4F4F4
Warm white, softer than pure white and less sterile, more like a kitchen.
Stone #F2F0EC
Surface colour for cards, chips and inputs. Neutral, without feeling cold.
Terracotta #C6654C
A single accent colour, warm and food-adjacent, not generic. Used only for CTAs and key moments.
Ink #323232
Warm near-black, softer than pure black and kinder on tired eyes.
Why not blue? Blue felt too generic and a little clinical. Terracotta feels more personal, warmer and more like Easey.

04. Interactive Prototype

Tap through the complete user journey

From the first onboarding screen to the home dashboard, this is the full flow as designed. Each screen was built in Figma and polished for the final prototype.

  • 1Onboarding sets the tone by acknowledging that feeling of being too tired.
  • 2Soft login, with no pressure to sign up right away.
  • 3Quick preference setup, with just your name and diet type.
  • 4Home, where you can share your mood and scan or type what you have in the fridge.
  • 5One recipe, no scrolling, just cook.
